dashboard-king-systems-2020-06-16.question: Our medical device plant in Indiana is a major source of HAP. On the breathing-circuit assembly lines we bond polymer sub-assemblies by applying methylene chloride so the plastic softens and fuses as the solvent evaporates; nothing with solids is applied and no dry film is left behind. We are adding six more of these lines. Does the NESHAP for surface coating of plastic parts cover this solvent welding step?

dashboard-ames-copper-2020-08-14.question: We are proposing a copper recovery plant in North Carolina permitted as a synthetic minor (area source) for HAP. Scrap tubing, wire, radiators and brass casings are sorted to at least 90 percent copper, melted in a natural-gas-fired tilting anode furnace with silica and lime flux, oxidized with air, reduced with natural gas and cast into 99.7 percent copper anodes that are shipped off site for refining. There is no sweating or burning of insulation. Is this facility a secondary copper smelter under the area source NESHAP?

dashboard-jackson-cleaners-2020-08-06.question: We run a small perchloroethylene dry cleaning shop in Michigan. There is an apartment above the shop that is currently unoccupied, and the machine is often idle because the location is mainly a pick-up and drop-off store. Does the requirement to eliminate perc emissions from dry cleaning systems located in a building with a residence after December 21, 2020 apply to us?

dashboard-vicor-2020-04-16.question: Our Massachusetts plant is an area source of HAP and makes modular power supplies and power conversion components for aerospace, defense and computing customers. We are classified under SIC 3679 (electronic components, not elsewhere classified) and NAICS 335999. Are we covered by the area source NESHAP for metal fabrication and finishing?

dashboard-genesis-alkali-westvaco-2021-0.question: Our Wyoming trona (soda ash) plant is a major source of HAP. In the caustic recovery loop we run a lime slaker and a natural-gas-fired lime kiln that calcines calcium carbonate lime mud back into quicklime for reuse in the process; we do not process limestone and do not sell lime. Does the NESHAP for lime manufacturing plants apply to our kiln?

dashboard-citation-oil-gas-2021-02-11.question: At our gas plant in Utah, an area source of HAP, we operate three existing 800 hp four-stroke lean-burn natural gas engines that have met the geographic criteria for a remote location since October 2013. We never sent the state a notification of remote status. Can we meet the work practice standards for remote engines instead of doing performance tests?

dashboard-palisades-nuclear-2021-02-02.question: Our nuclear power station in Michigan is an area source of HAP. An audit found two 500-gallon gasoline tanks and one 500-gallon diesel tank used only to fuel company vehicles; none of them are in our operating permit. Are these tanks covered by the area source NESHAP for gasoline dispensing facilities?

dashboard-cemex-knoxville-2021-04-30.question: At our Portland cement plant in Tennessee we divert kiln exhaust to dry pulverized coal in the coal mill, which exhausts through its own stack. We believe the coal mill falls only under the cement NESHAP and not under the NSPS for coal preparation plants. Which particulate limits and compliance demonstrations apply to the coal mill stack?

dashboard-us-granules-henrietta-2022-03-.question: Our Missouri plant recovers aluminum from coated scrap by heating it in delamination chambers to burn off paint and plastic, then grinds it into aluminum granules. We do not melt aluminum and our customers tell us they do not melt the granules either. Does the secondary aluminum NESHAP apply to the delamination units?

dashboard-tesla-denver-2020-12-14.question: We operate a vehicle service and body repair center in Denver, an area source, where we spray apply refinish coatings to cars. None of the coatings we spray contain the target metal HAP (chromium, lead, manganese, nickel or cadmium) and we can certify that. We occasionally use methylene chloride paint stripper. Can we be exempted from the area source auto body coating requirements?

dashboard-hartford-finishing-2021-02-16.question: We are a contract coating shop in Wisconsin, an area source, coating metal parts for other manufacturers. One line (a polyurea line) spray applies a coating that contains none of the target HAP metals, while other lines do use them. Is that polyurea line subject to the area source surface coating NESHAP?

dashboard-texas-eastern-somerset-2023-05.question: We run a lean premix gas-fired combustion turbine at a natural gas compressor station in Ohio, a major source of HAP. The unit was built after 2003 and has no oxidation catalyst. We want to show compliance with the formaldehyde limit by monitoring gas producer turbine speed and inlet air temperature instead of installing a catalyst. Is that allowed and what must we submit?

dashboard-buchanan-marine-2023-04-10.question: Our Connecticut marine railway used to build barges but since 2011 only repairs them: dry abrasive blasting, welding and spray coating of steel hulls, staying under 3,000 gallons a year of coatings and solvents as an area source. We are now classified as ship building and repairing (SIC 3731, NAICS 336611). Does the area source NESHAP for metal fabrication and finishing still apply?

dashboard-seepex-2024-01-25.question: Our Ohio facility, an area source, assembles and repairs progressive cavity pumps (SIC 3561) from components bought elsewhere. We do some spot welding, dry machining, dry grinding, abrasive blasting and spray painting, but fewer than half of the pumps go through those finishing steps. Are we 'primarily engaged' in a covered metal fabrication and finishing category?

dashboard-materion-brush-2023-05-31.question: At our beryllium products plant in Ohio we use two diesel engines mounted on portable vacuum units that are moved around the site to clean up beryllium-containing material. Are these engines stationary engines subject to the RICE NESHAP?

dashboard-eaton-auburn-2023-09-07.question: Our Indiana plant tests heavy-duty clutches. Seven diesel truck engines of 335 to 600 hp, supplied by engine manufacturers, sit in dynamometer test cells for years and drive the clutch under test through a straight shaft. We think the engine test cell exemptions in the engine rules cover us. Are these engines exempt from the stationary engine NESHAP?

dashboard-dte-greenwood-2023-10-24.question: Our Michigan power plant has one electric generating boiler permitted for natural gas and fuel oil. Oil is burned only during startup: well under 10 percent of heat input on a three-year average and under 15 percent in any single year. Is this unit covered by the utility mercury and air toxics rule or by the major source boiler MACT?

dashboard-corteva-midland-2023-12-12.question: At our Michigan chemical site, a major source of HAP, we make a 2,4-D phenoxy herbicide active ingredient. We want to add a distillation column to strip water from a purchased raw material (70 to 80 percent purity) so it feeds the herbicide unit at 99 percent purity; the raw material is stored in existing tanks in a neighboring building. Which organic chemical NESHAP would the new distillation process fall under?

adi-M200005.question: We are building a lithium-ion battery cell plant in Michigan that will be an area source of HAP. The cathode line mixes nickel-containing active material, binder and NMP solvent into a slurry that is coated onto foil and dried. Which area source NESHAP applies to the cathode slurry mixing process?

adi-Z200004.question: Our Alabama plant makes glass frit (NAICS 3255) by melting nickel-containing raw materials and quenching the melt into frit used in ceramic glazes and coatings; we are an area source. Between the chemical preparations rule, the paints and allied products rule and the chemical manufacturing area source rule, which one covers frit production?

adi-M200007.question: At our secondary aluminum plant in Ohio we want to install a thermal chip dryer running at about 660 degrees F to drive water off shredded aluminum that carries some paint before the shreds go to the melting furnace. We believe that temperature is too low to form hydrocarbons or dioxins. Would the dryer be an affected source under the secondary aluminum NESHAP?

adi-M200004.question: Two residual-oil-fired utility boilers at our New Hampshire station are sometimes fired only to make auxiliary steam, for example to heat the on-site fuel oil tanks, without generating electricity. Can we treat that operation as startup under the utility mercury and air toxics rule so the startup work practices apply instead of the emission limits?

adi-M150020.question: Unit 1 at our Connecticut power station is a 4,286 MMBtu per hour steam boiler that burns No. 2 and No. 4 fuel oil as its main fuel with only a small amount of natural gas, and it runs at a low annual capacity factor. Does it qualify as a limited-use liquid oil-fired unit under the utility mercury and air toxics rule?

adi-M190019.question: At our Michigan site we plan an epoxy dispersion process that makes a coating product; the final step filters the finished product to remove lumps and gels. If that filtering counts as a 'separation activity', we think the coatings manufacturing NESHAP would not apply and the miscellaneous organic chemical NESHAP might instead. How should we classify this process?

adi-M170002.question: At our Colorado refinery, vapors from the truck loading rack in Plant 2 go to an enclosed vapor combustor. Is that combustor considered a flare under the petroleum refinery NESHAP, so that the refinery flare monitoring requirements apply to it?

adi-M160007.question: Our Virginia plant makes mica sheet insulation. On one line mica paper is fed from a roll through a coating line; on the other line the material is handled as sheets. Is either line a web coating line, and are the finished mica insulation products refractory products under the refractory NESHAP?

adi-M170004.question: At our natural gas transmission facility in New Mexico, a major source, the glycol dehydration unit is regulated under the gas transmission and storage NESHAP, with the still vent routed to a flare. The reboiler that heats the glycol burns field gas and its combustion exhaust goes straight to the atmosphere. Is the reboiler burner also a process heater under the boiler and process heater MACT?

adi-M160020.question: Our Michigan steel plant, an area source, melts scrap in an electric arc furnace and turns the molten steel into shot and grit through a water atomization process rather than pouring it into sand molds. Trade groups call our product castings. Should we be regulated as an iron and steel foundry area source instead of as an electric arc furnace steelmaking area source?

adi-M150031.question: Our municipal utility in Louisiana has three natural-gas-fired electric generating boilers at an area source. They are permitted to burn fuel oil only during gas curtailment and for a limited number of test hours each year. Are these boilers subject to the area source boiler rule?

adi-M150028.question: Our Arkansas fiberboard plant runs a closed-loop gasification system: rotary gasifiers and a secondary combustion chamber burn wood residue, and most of the hot gas flows directly through the fiber dryers, which comply with the plywood and composite wood products NESHAP. Some hot gas bypasses the dryers to heat thermal oil. Since the dryers are covered by the wood products rule, is the whole gasification system exempt from the boiler and process heater MACT?

adi-M160002.question: Our Virginia sawmill plans to raise lumber production so that methanol emissions from the lumber dry kilns would exceed 10 tons per year, which would make us a major source of HAP. Would the plywood and composite wood products NESHAP then apply to us, and would the kilns become affected sources as soon as the revised permit reclassifying us is issued?

adi-M160009.question: Our pharmaceutical plant in Ohio took federally enforceable limits on organic HAP before the chemical manufacturing area source rule took effect, so we are an area source. We now operate control devices, but even without them we would stay below the major source thresholds. Does the Title V permit requirement in that area source rule apply to us?
